body:
Source: the release review of v1.11.1..main. scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs is the guard that forbids test files from leaving mkdtempSync fixtures behind. It had four gaps.
- It scanned comments and string literals as code, so a commented or quoted `mkdtempSync(` produced a false leak report (or a false removal), with no sanctioned exception because ALLOWLIST is locked at zero.
- Its bare-assignment binding rule (`let dir; before(() => { dir = mkdtempSync(...) })`) and the rule that a member assignment (`ctx.dir = mkdtempSync(...)`) stays unbound had no planted-shape test.
- It counted textual creation sites against removal sites, so a factory helper with one mkdtempSync whose callers sometimes skipped removal passed: packages/gate-manifest/test/key-ceremony-cli.test.mjs leaked three directories per run this way.
- Its header claimed every leak fails the guard, while it only sees mkdtempSync fixtures in suite directories.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. Comments and the contents of string, template and regex literals are blanked (newlines and length kept, so reported line numbers stay right) before matching; code inside `${...}` is still scanned.
2. A mkdtempSync result returned from its enclosing function (returned directly, through realpathSync/resolve/normalize, or inside a returned object or array literal) counts as removed only when the removal is registered inside that function (t.after, or a module-level registry drained by after()).
3. Every suite file the stricter rule flags is fixed, never exempted: each factory adds its fixture to a module-level registry drained in after(), and key-ceremony-cli.test.mjs uses tmp(t).
4. The header states exactly what the guard covers and what it does not (mkdirSync under tmpdir, async mkdtemp, mktemp, files outside suite directories), and that test-kit fixtures are covered because tmp()/gitRepo() refuse to run without a test context.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 Planted tests pin the bare-assignment rule (removed and not removed) and the member-assignment rule. verify: `node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs`
- AC2 A commented or quoted `mkdtempSync(` is not reported, a quoted `rmSync(dir` is not a removal, and a call inside an interpolation is still found. verify: `node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs`
- AC3 A factory with one creation site and a caller that skips removal is reported; t.after and registry factories are not. verify: `node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs`
- AC4 The guard is green on the whole tree with ALLOWLIST still empty, and key-ceremony-cli leaves no directory behind. verify: `node --test scripts/test/tmp-fixture-boundary.test.mjs packages/gate-manifest/test/key-ceremony-cli.test.mjs`
- AC5 Every changed suite still passes. verify: `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep test.mjs | xargs node --test`

OUT OF SCOPE: detecting fixtures made with mkdirSync under tmpdir, async mkdtemp or mktemp; freezing the guard file as a trust root (separate change).
title: tmp-fixture-boundary: see through comments and strings, pin its binding rules, and require helpers that return a fixture to register its removal
